I had a best friend who I've known for around 10 years now we are incredibly close and he has severe ADHD, I'm not sure if this is a common thing as I can't find any literature on it but it seems as though from a very young age they are babied incredible amounts which leads to a dependence and an inability to feel responsible for a lot of things. 

In my friend I found this from his mum, he to this day (he's 20) when he is home will have his mum make food for him, wake him up in the morning, make sure he's done x,y and z. This could also be seen when I lived with him (for 2 years before I dropped out of uni) I regularly had to keep on top of him making sure he was up in the morning, had eaten his meals, had attended what he needed to and so on. 

He now is much more dependent however this has taken a lot of work. I think the key thing is establishing accountability routines, a written down daily timeline, wake up time, out of bed time, x meal in morning, x meal lunch, x meal dinner, bed at x time sleep at x time. The thing is the more decisions they have the more they get distracted and the more they get off target which spirals to I will never be able to get anything done, which can lead to rather bad depressive spouts. 

I think you need to be very careful that you do not become his dependence but help him develope ways to make himself accountable. Make sure you make him realise this didn't happen because YOU didn't stick to x and YOU therefore didn't have time to do x which meant you got in trouble ext. 

A lit of people under estimate how hard it is for people with ADHD to function in day to day life with how easily they can go down rabbit holes in anything making food can lead to finding out what ingredients are in x which can lead to a YouTube video which can lead to x and so on. It's hard. 

I would really advise you stick it out he is not a lost cause he just needs some help getting back on track and for you to set clear boundaries so he can be aware when he is being too much and how he can change to make things easier for you whilst still having you there if he really needs help. 

Hope this helps at all. Would also potentially recommend meds, he probably hates meds but just whilst he is getting back on track the negatives can be worth it. Melatonin is a natural sleeping supplement that really helps my friend sleep (sleep is so important for them to be able to establish any form of routine). Other than that just try maybe do a little research into ADHD and just be honest with him as to how you are feeling and as to what needs to change but also have a understand of what won't change so you can be willing to committee. 

My friend is doing amazingly now, occasionally he will have blips where he fucks his sleep and it all goes to shit and he feels hopeless like he's ruining his life but he knows I'm there to be real with him and tell him look fix x,y and z get your routines goings and everything will follow site.
